BiblicalUsage: maqqâchâh is merchandise, something received in trade, and it occurs once, in Nehemiah 10:31. There the people promise that if traders bring ware or victuals on the Sabbath to sell, they will not buy it of them on the Sabbath or the holy day. The word is the market held outside the Sabbath.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe maqqâchâh shows me that even honest trade must wait for the Sabbath, and that rest is worth more than a bargain.
